name: BACH_0399
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (68%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Image sits at the 100th OOD percentile, and the 90% set holds three classes.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 68%, Invasive 24%, Benign 7% | InSitu leads |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu, Invasive | Three classes remain |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.11 / 100th percentile | Input flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Top classes differ |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 InSitu | Mixed; nearest two Invasive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Benign stroma or fat** (region 4) · ↑ invasive · Scarce; concept model links this to invasive [F3] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined in ducts** (regions 2, 8) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Weak
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 2, 9, 11) · context · 73% of nuclei neoplastic, 97th percentile [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Top-3 removal drops invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Unreliable here: normal lobules (0/20), necrosis (3/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Reliability is 0.11 and the second model disagrees, so even the InSitu lead may not hold.
- TIL concept is high, yet HoVer-Net found no immune nuclei in sampled regions 2, 9, 11.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 6, 5, 10:** top heatmap contribution toward invasive; look for stromal invasion.
2. **Region 9:** strongest tumor-infiltrating stroma score (validated); check for invasive foci.
3. **Regions 2, 8:** look for atypical cells confined within ducts.
